newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian farmers vow to keep up protests.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers vow to keep up protests.

text.p: Italian farmers vowed to keep up protests which have blocked roads to Milan's Linate airport for the past two days after a meeting with the government failed to meet their demands on Saturday.

More than 1,000 farmers took part in the third day of protests in the northern city of Milan against a draft law which they say does not compensate them enough for milk output cuts imposed by the European Union.
They blocked roads to Linate with cows and tractors, forcing passengers coming from central Milan to walk three km (two miles) to reach the international airport.
The farmers promised to keep up their protests for as long as possible after a meeting with agriculture ministry officials in Milan did not solve the problem.

"We are going to keep this up. I hope more farmers come from all around," one farmer said. State television said farmers were also considering blocking roads to Milan's San Siro football stadium where Italian first division clubs Internazionale play Bologna on Sunday.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi, in Venice for private talks with Spanish counterpart Jose Maria Aznar, said he sympathised with farmers' plight but Italy had to obey European Union laws.
"The Italian government is firmly committed to giving relief to farmers, but it cannot disobey European Union rules, which constitute a framework we are obliged to obey," Prodi told reporters.
The farmers say the draft law fell short of their demands for the state to help bear the burden of EU "super levy" fines for overproduction.
Media reports say Italian farmers face 420 billion lire ($270 million) in EU fines for overproduction. Estimates from member states rank Italy as the worst offender for exceeding its national quota.
Late last year, an EU Commission official said milk production in the 15-member bloc was 1.1 million tonnes over quota, with Italy accounting for 470,000 tonnes, nearly half.
The fines hit individual farmers and not the state. Farmers want the government to ensure that they do not have to shoulder the full burden themselves.
